title: ShellBench: What Matters More for AI Agents, Models, or Harness for Everyday Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2611.32946v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The use of AI agents among the general public has been increasing exponentially throughout 2026, though it is often hard for users to determine which configuration is most effective for their personal use. To help provide clarity here we introduce ShellBench, 100 day-to-day tasks based on more than 10 million user requests, each set in a realistic workspace with messy files and competing data sources, and graded for both correctness and safety. We evaluate 12 models across 5 agent harnesses at 3 reasoning levels for a total of 53,100 rollouts, 20% of which are on tasks designated for public release. We find that model choice impacts performance more than harness choice, but the three leading models differ by only 1.1 percentage points. GPT-6.1 Sol passed 61.4% of attempts at about one-sixth of GPT-6 Astra's estimated token cost per attempt, while GPT-6 Astra led at 62.5%. We also found that harness choice had little effect on either perf

translated_title: ShellBench：对于AI智能体的日常任务而言，模型和智能体框架哪个更重要？
translated_abstract: 2026年全年，AI智能体在普通大众中的使用呈指数级增长，但用户往往难以确定哪种配置对其个人使用最为有效。为了帮助澄清这一问题，我们推出了ShellBench——基于超过1000万条用户请求构建的100项日常任务基准，每项任务都设置在包含杂乱文件和相互冲突数据源的真实工作空间中，并对正确性和安全性进行双重评分。我们评估了12个模型在5种智能体框架和3个推理水平下的表现，总计进行了53,100次实验，其中20%的任务被指定为公开发布。我们发现，模型选择对性能的影响大于框架选择，但三个领先模型之间的差距仅为1.1个百分点。GPT-6.1 Sol以约GPT-6 Astra每次尝试估算token成本的六分之一通过了61.4%的尝试，而GPT-6 Astra以62.5%的通过率位居首位。我们还发现，框架选择对性能几乎没有影响。
tldr: 该论文推出ShellBench基准，通过对12个模型、5种智能体框架和3个推理水平共53,100次实验的评估发现，模型选择对日常任务性能的影响大于框架选择，但领先模型之间差距仅1.1个百分点，且高性能模型间的成本差异可达六倍之多。
en_tdlr: ShellBench, a benchmark of 100 everyday tasks built from over 10 million user requests, reveals through 53,100 evaluations that model choice matters more than harness choice for AI agent performance on everyday tasks, though the top three models differ by only 1.1 percentage points.
